_meta.indication: Prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in patients 13 years of age and older who are at high risk of developing these infections due to being severely immunocompromised, such as HSCT recipients with GVHD or those with hematologic malignancies with prolonged neutropenia from chemotherapy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 1 / C/I98-316 (posaconazole vs fluconazole in HSCT recipients with GVHD)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled: posaconazole oral suspension 200 mg three times a day vs fluconazole capsules 400 mg once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Allogeneic HSCT recipients with Graft versus Host Disease (GVHD) receiving high-dose immunosuppressive therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite endpoint of clinical failure (breakthrough proven/probable invasive fungal infection, mortality, and use of systemic antifungal therapy) through 16 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success 202/301 (67%) posaconazole vs 189/299 (63%) fluconazole; 95.01% CI for the difference in success rates (-2.7, 12.2). All-cause mortality at 16 weeks similar: POS 58/301 (19%) vs FLU 59/299 (20%)

nct_ctgov.title: Prophylaxis Trial in High Risk Allogenic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients With Graft vs. Host Disease

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 2 / P01899 (posaconazole vs fluconazole/itraconazole in neutropenic patients)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label (evaluator-blind), active-controlled: posaconazole oral suspension 200 mg three times a day vs fluconazole suspension 400 mg once daily or itraconazole oral solution 200 mg twice a day
pivotal_trials.population: Neutropenic patients receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy for acute myelogenous leukemia or myelodysplastic syndromes
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite endpoint of clinical failure (breakthrough proven/probable invasive fungal infection, mortality, and use of systemic antifungal therapy) at end of oral therapy plus 7 days
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success 166 (55%) posaconazole vs 126 (42%) fluconazole/itraconazole; 95.13% CI for the difference (4.3, 20.1). All-cause mortality at 100 days lower with posaconazole: POS 44/304 (14%) vs FLU/ITZ 64/298 (21%)

nct_ctgov.title: Prophylaxis Trial of Posaconazole Versus Standard Azole Therapy for Neutropenic Patients (Study P01899)

key_safety: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (at least 10% in the POS or FLU groups, pooled prophylaxis safety analysis) included fever (45%), diarrhea (42%), nausea (38%), vomiting (29%), headache (28%), abdominal pain (27%). Most serious concerns were hepatic toxicity (elevated LFTs, rare severe liver injury) and QTc prolongation.
target_moa: Triazole antifungal that blocks synthesis of ergosterol, a key component of the fungal cell membrane, by inhibiting the enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase

description.text: Added treatment of invasive aspergillosis indication and expanded pediatric use (2 years and older, 10 kg or greater) with the new Noxafil PowderMix for delayed-release oral suspension formulation

summary.text: NDA 22-003 for Noxafil (posaconazole) oral suspension was granted a priority review and approved for prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in severely immunocompromised patients 13 years and older, based on two Phase 3 active-controlled prophylaxis studies (C/I98-316 and P01899).
